01 / 24

AutoSDLC takes a software idea in one sentence and carries it through planning, analysis, design, review, development, testing, deployment and maintenance. A separate AI agent runs each stage. At the end I will talk about the errors we ran into and what we learned from them.

Problem

Why is “write me an app”
not enough for an LLM?

User

Write me an event registration app.

Model

Here are 400 lines of code! Good luck.

No requirements

We cannot measure whether it did the right thing.

No tests

Nobody knows whether the code works.

No documents

Architecture decisions get lost in the chat.

Hard to change

A small request makes it rewrite everything.

Real projects have a process around the code: the SDLC.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents02 / 24

Generating code from a single prompt is nice for a demo, but without requirements, tests and documents we cannot tell whether it is right. When we ask for a change, the model usually rewrites everything. The idea: apply the SDLC stages we learned in software engineering to agents.

Connected with CrewAI Flows: every agent reads the documents of the stages before it.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents03 / 24

There are eight agents, each with its own role and goal. Each produces a Markdown document or code. The stages are connected: the Design Agent reads the requirements, the Test Agent writes tests from the requirements and builds a traceability matrix.

Technology

The technologies
we used

CrewAI Flows

Python framework that runs the agents and the order of the stages.

OpenCode Go

The model gateway. Default model glm-5.3-flash; each stage can use its own model.

Streamlit

Live UI: stage status, agent output, questions, document editing.

SQLite

Run history, events, versions and change requests.

Playwright + pytest

API and UI tests of the generated project, with a real Chromium.

Docker + Dokploy

How both AutoSDLC and the apps it generates are deployed.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents04 / 24

The generator is Python, but the projects it creates can be Node.js, Go, Rust or Python; web, CLI or desktop. The Docker image has all these toolchains, because the tests of the generated code run in the same container.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents05 / 24

Three layers. The interface starts jobs and shows the events from SQLite live. The orchestration layer runs the stages in order and checks the agent outputs. In the workspace the generated project is really installed, its tests run and its server starts. The model never runs code; our code runs it and measures the result.

A short look at the code

Agents and tasks are
defined in YAML

config/agents.yaml (shortened)

review:
  role: Architecture Review Agent
  goal: Independently audit the design
    against the requirements.
  backstory: A senior architect who catches
    missing requirements before any
    code is written.

testing:
  role: Test Agent
  goal: Prepare API, UI and unit tests
    that match the requirements.

config/tasks.yaml (shortened)

review:
  description: |
    Project idea: $idea
    The design to review: $context
    Write the whole report in $language.
    Findings: | No | Severity | Finding |
    Critical or High finding → REVISE.
    The last line must be exactly
    "VERDICT: APPROVE" or "VERDICT: REVISE".
  expected_output: A review report
    with a findings table and a VERDICT line.

Prompts live apart from the code: adding or changing an agent needs no Python. The application fills the variables that start with $. Prompts are in English; $language chooses the document language.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents06 / 24

In CrewAI an agent is defined by three things: its role, its goal and its backstory. A task says what to do and what output is expected. We keep them in YAML files. Note the review task: we ask the model to end with a verdict line that a program can read, because the next step is done by code.

A short look at the code

From agent to agent:
CrewAI Flow

runner.py · stage order (shortened)

class SDLCFlow(Flow):
    @start()
    def plan(self):
        return session.execute("planning", ...)

    @listen(plan)
    def analyse(self, _previous):
        return session.execute("analysis", ...)

    @listen(analyse)
    def design(self, _previous): ...

    # review → develop → test → deploy → maintain

runner.py · stage inputs

# which documents does each agent read?
STAGE_INPUTS = {
  "analysis":    ("planning",),
  "design":      ("analysis", "planning"),
  "review":      ("design", "analysis"),
  "development": ("design", "analysis",
                  "review"),
  "testing":     ("analysis", "design"),
}

@listen: when a stage ends, the next one starts. Earlier documents go into the prompt's $context.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents07 / 24

The agents do not talk to each other directly. The Flow starts the next stage when one finishes. STAGE_INPUTS decides what an agent knows: for example the Development Agent sees the design, the requirements and the review report. The user's answers and decisions are added to every prompt's context too.

A short look at the code

How does
an agent call work?

crewai_engine.py · _ask() (simplified)

prompt = Template(task["description"]).substitute(
    idea=idea, context=context, language="English")

agent = Agent(role=cfg["role"], goal=cfg["goal"],
              backstory=cfg["backstory"], llm=llm,
              allow_delegation=False, max_iter=3)
task = Task(description=prompt, agent=agent,
            expected_output=task["expected_output"])
raw = Crew(agents=[agent], tasks=[task]).kickoff().raw

if raw.startswith("USER_QUESTION:"):
    raise ClarificationNeeded(...)  # a question in the UI

1. Prompt

The YAML template is filled with the idea, the context and the language.

2. Agent + Task + Crew

Every stage is a small crew with one agent. Delegation is off.

3. Model

The OpenCode Go gateway; each stage can use its own model.

4. Question

On USER_QUESTION: the run stops; the answer is added to the context.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents08 / 24

This function is the common entry point of every stage. It fills the prompt from YAML, builds the CrewAI Agent and Task and runs them. We turned delegation off: we wanted the routing to be explicit in the code, not agents handing work to each other. If the model notices a missing decision it returns a question in a fixed format, and we show it to the user in the UI.

How it works

The agents
check each other

Review loop

  1. The Review Agent compares the design with the requirements.
  2. The report contains a verdict line: VERDICT: APPROVE or REVISE.
  3. On REVISE the Design Agent fixes the findings.

at most 2 rounds, then it moves on

Test / repair loop

  1. The tests really run.
  2. The failure output goes back to the right agent.
  3. A repair that breaks passing tests is rolled back.
  4. More passing tests each attempt earn extra attempts.

2 repairs by default + 2 extra attempts

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents09 / 24

We do not expect the right result in one pass. The Review Agent can reject the design; then the Design Agent fixes it. When tests fail, their output is given back to an agent. An important detail: if a repair breaks tests that passed before, we roll it back, so we never lose a good state.

A short look at the code

Routing back:
review → design

runner.py · review() (shortened)

def review(self):
    for number in range(1, MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS + 1):  # 2 rounds
        report = self._generate("review")
        if review_verdict(report) == "APPROVE":
            break
        # REVISE: the findings go to the Design Agent
        self.docs["design"] = self._generate("design",
            "ARCHITECTURE REVIEW FINDINGS — revise the "
            "existing design only where these findings "
            "require it:" + report,
            base=self.docs["design"])

Verdict line

The VERDICT (or Turkish KARAR) line is read with a regex.

The Design Agent runs again

It gets the old design with the findings; only what is needed changes.

Same idea in testing

The failure output goes to the Development or the Test Agent.

The code does the routing,
not the model.
AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents10 / 24

This is how work goes back from one agent to another. The code reads the verdict line in the Review Agent's report. On REVISE it calls the Design Agent again with the findings. There are at most two rounds, otherwise it could loop forever. The repair loop in testing works the same way.

How it works

A human is still
in the loop

Impact Analysis Agent

If an event is full and you are registered: should “Full” and “Registered” show together?

User

Show both of them.

Questions and answers

On an unclear decision the agent stops and asks.

Section editing

A change comes as a diff; accept or reject it.

Retry and model choice

After a failure, from the same stage, with another model if wanted.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents11 / 24

This is the real question asked while applying CR-003. Instead of deciding on its own at an unclear point, the agent asks, and the answer is passed to the later stages. We can also edit a single section of a document; the change is shown as a diff.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents12 / 24

When we want a new feature after the project is generated, we do not regenerate everything. The Impact Analysis Agent uses the traceability matrix to find the affected requirements, files and tests. Only those stages run again; the rest are skipped. We added three changes to the event app this way.

Errors we ran into

We learned the most
from the errors

1

Model: it keeps thinking, repeats the same line, switches language.

2

Tests: is a red test the code's fault or the test's?

3

Turkish: a button not found because of the letter “İ”.

4

Frameworks: the version the model knows is old.

5

Infrastructure: a library update, timeouts, retry.

Every error came back into the system as a check and a test.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents15 / 24

In agent systems the real work is writing the checks that catch the model's mistakes. I grouped them under five headings; the next slides show an example and its fix for each.

Errors we ran into

Error 1: the model
keeps thinking

Maintenance Agent, a Turkish document

## 9. Bakım
Bil الإنسan discharge了打工作报告 планируемый …

Endless reasoning for minutes

Fix: a 60,000-character budget, then “answer now”. If it still does not, the stage stops and suggests another model.

Repeating a line a loop

Fix: the repeating output is cut and asked once more.

Language drift other scripts

Fix: a script the prompt does not use makes us ask again.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents16 / 24

The text on the left is a real example: the model, which had to write Turkish, suddenly drifted into Arabic, Chinese and Russian words. Some models also thought for minutes without answering. We put a measurable limit on each and give the model a clear warning when it is crossed.

Errors we ran into

Error 2: a red test,
whose fault?

The test's own code is broken syntax, wrong helper

→ back to the Test Agent.

The app said 400, the request was invalid

→ to the Test Agent, with the server's reason.

A real behavior bug

→ to the Development Agent, with the failing tests.

A repair broke passing tests

→ rolled back; the broken tests are named to the developer.

At first

Every failure went to the Development Agent. It “fixed” correct code and broke it.

Giving the error to the right agent,
in concrete form,
made the biggest difference.
AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents17 / 24

At first we gave every test failure to the developer. But often the test itself was wrong, and the agent broke correct code to make the test pass. Once we classified the failures and sent them to the right agent, the success rate went up a lot.

Errors we ran into

Error 3: the “İptal” button
is not found

tests/ui/registration.test.js (written by the Test Agent)

page.getByRole('button',
  { name: /iptal/i })

// the button on screen: "İptal"
// result: no match ✗

Why?

In JavaScript the /i flag does not match the Turkish “İ” (U+0130) with “i”.

The second trap

Python's re.I does match it, so our check written in Python did not see the error.

Fix

The build check imitates JavaScript and warns before the tests run.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents18 / 24

This error is specific to a Turkish UI. “İptal” means Cancel. The tests passed with the English UI but could not find the Cancel button in Turkish. When we first wrote the check, Python's regex behaved differently, so we did not catch it. Now we handle the letter İ explicitly.

Errors we ran into

Error 4: the model writes code
from old knowledge

SymptomCauseFix
TypeError: Cannot set property queryIn Express 5 req.query is read-only.The build check catches it; a clear instruction to the agent.
#email not foundantd Form name="login" gives the input the id login_email.Ids in the tests are compared with the UI code.
The tests never startA node:test file run with playwright test.The project.yaml commands are checked.
The server does not startRequired secrets (e.g. JWT_SECRET) are missing.The test server gets the secrets automatically.
AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents19 / 24

Models write code for the old versions in their training data. They do not know the changes in Express 5 or how Ant Design builds ids. We catch these quickly with static checks, without waiting minutes for the tests to run, and give the agent a clear message.

Errors we ran into

Error 5: sometimes
the infrastructure breaks

A library update HTTP 400

CrewAI 1.15 added a cache_breakpoint field to messages, and the gateway rejected the unknown field. Fix: only role and content are sent; a test was added.

Timeouts large projects

Installing packages and the test suite did not fit in 300 seconds. Fix: 1800 seconds.

Retry forgot the change CR “Failed”

Retrying a failed CR did a plain regeneration. Fix: retry reopens the CR first.

UI language Streamlit

The language went back to English after a page switch; a template filled English text into the Turkish form. Fix: the language choice is kept in session state.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents20 / 24

Not every error comes from the model. A library update broke every call; timeouts were too short for large projects; and the UI had classic Streamlit bugs. For each fix we wrote a test so it does not come back.

Conclusion

What we learned

1

The model is not deterministic; the checks around it must be.

2

Give concrete errors: file, line, the server's answer.

3

Keep the good state: roll back a fix that breaks things.

4

Every error becomes a test: no error comes twice.

5

Ask a human when unsure: instead of guessing.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents21 / 24

In short: LLMs are powerful but unreliable. The way to use them in a reliable process is to measure their output, give errors back clearly and ask a human where they are not sure.

Conclusion

Limits and
next steps

today

Limits

One shared password, no separation between users.

Generated code runs in the container; do not deploy it without a review.

Small and medium projects.

Fast models need more repair rounds.

next

Next steps

Isolation per user.

More stacks (Java, .NET).

Token and cost tracking.

Git integration: every CR a pull request.

AutoSDLC · SDLC with AI agents22 / 24

This is a PoC, not a product for production. A human has to review the generated code. User isolation and git integration are the most sensible next steps.

Closing

The goal is not to have AI write code,
but to run the process

Requirements, design, code, tests and documents; connected and traceable, with eight agents and one human.

Appendix

“What was a US?”
terms

SDLC
Software Development Life Cycle: the stages from planning to maintenance.
agent
A software component driven by an LLM, with a role, a goal and tools.
LLM
Large Language Model: a model that generates text (e.g. GLM, Kimi).
CrewAI Flow
A Python structure that connects agents and steps in order.
FR / NFR
Functional / Non-Functional Requirement: what it does and how well.
US / AC
User Story and Acceptance Criteria.
traceability
Which design, file and test every requirement is linked to.
repair loop
After a failing test the code is fixed and the tests run again.
CR
Change Request: a change added to the project later.
delta mode
In a CR, only the affected stages run again.
reasoning budget
How many characters a model may think before it answers.
build check
Static checks for known mistakes, before the tests run.
